questions.q: What are the three lifecycle stages a customer relationship moves through, in order?
options: Sales, marketing, support
Marketing, sales, service
Service, sales, marketing
Billing, sales, marketing
questions.explain: Marketing generates interest, sales converts it into a signed deal, and service keeps the customer successful afterward.

questions.q: What is a 'lead,' as defined in this lesson?
options: A signed customer with an active contract
A support ticket that has already been resolved
A person who has shown interest but hasn't been qualified as a sales opportunity yet
A marketing email template
questions.explain: A lead is produced by marketing activity — someone who showed interest, like filling out a form, before being qualified for a sales conversation.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say a sales-ready handoff from marketing matters?
options: Because marketing is legally required to approve every call
Because leads automatically become opportunities with no review
Because sales reps are not allowed to contact leads directly
Because calling someone who isn't actually ready for a sales conversation wastes everyone's time
questions.explain: Not every lead is ready for a sales conversation — organizations define what makes a lead sales-ready before handing it over.

questions.q: What does this lesson say happens when a service team has no record of a customer's purchase or sales history?
options: The customer automatically receives a refund
The customer ends up repeating their own story to every new person they talk to
The case is instantly resolved without any agent involvement
Nothing changes, since service doesn't need that context
questions.explain: A service team that doesn't know a customer's history recreates the exact problem described in Lesson 1 — the customer has to start over.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is CRM actually built to solve across the lifecycle?
options: Replacing marketing, sales, and service teams with a single employee
Making sure only one team ever touches a given customer
Eliminating the need for any handoffs between teams
Keeping one continuous, trustworthy record as a person moves from stranger to lead to opportunity to customer
questions.explain: Each stage isn't hard to imagine as a separate tool — what's hard is the continuity across the handoffs, which is exactly what a shared system provides.
